'''Edward Arthur''' "'''Peter'''" '''Robinson''' (1933 – July 2026) was a British-Canadian [[chemist]] and professor [[emeritus]] at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]]. He played a significant role in the establishment the university's Mississauga campus (originally known as Erindale College) in the 1960s and 70s, acting as its first associate dean, and later as [[Dean (education)|dean]] and [[List of principals of the University of Toronto Mississauga|principal]].

==Biography==
Robinson was born in 1933 in [[England]] and attended [[Alleyn's School]], a [[grammar school]] in [[Dulwich]], London.<ref name=alleyns/> He went on to attend [[University College London]] and graduated with a [[bachelor of science]] degree in 1955 and a [[doctor of philosophy]] in 1958. He graduated with a [[doctor of science]] from the [[University of London]] in 1959.<ref name=oral_history/>

Robinson moved to [[Canada]] in 1958 as a post-doctoral fellow at [[McMaster University]] where he taught chemistry. He joined the [[University of Toronto]] in 1961 as an assistant professor in the Department of Chemistry at the St. George campus.<ref name=scholars/><ref>{{cite book |last1=Brook |first1=Adrian G. |last2=McBryde |first2=W.A.E. (Peter) |title=Historical Distillates : Chemistry at the University of Toronto since 1843 |publisher=Dundurn Press |location=Canada |isbn=9781550029161 |url=https://canadacommons.ca/artifacts/1868595/historical-distillates/2617657/view/}}</ref>

In 1966, he was asked by [[David Carlton Williams]], the vice-president for [[University of Toronto Mississauga|Erindale College]] and [[University of Toronto Scarborough|Scarborough College]] and principal of Erindale, to help organize the campus. During this time, Erindale had only 12 faculty and 150 students. Robinson began as associate dean in 1966 and saw the campus's establishment in 1967, remaining in the role until 1969.<ref>{{cite web |title=Farewell Principal Robinson - welcome Professor Robinson |url=https://www7.mississauga.ca/documents/library/biographies/Scans/Peel%20Biography%20Scans%20-%20R/Robinson,%20E.%20A.%20(Peter)%20MT%2019760519.pdf |website=mississauga.ca |publisher=City of Mississauga |access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> Robinson became its second dean that same year, following John S. Colman.<ref name=40yrs>{{cite web |last1=Percy |first1=John |last2=Abbas |first2=Sabeen |title=Celebrating 40 Years of History at the University of Toronto Mississauga |url=https://utoronto.scholaris.ca/items/06276dd4-2ced-489a-acb2-1af7904058ab |publisher=University of Toronto Mississauga |date=2007}}</ref>

In 1974, Robinson became Erindale's [[List of principals of the University of Toronto Mississauga|third principal]] after his close friend and predecessor [[John Tuzo Wilson]] left to become director general of the [[Ontario Science Centre]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McNicholl |first1=Martin K. |title=John Tuzo Wilson |url=https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/john-tuzo-wilson |website=The Canadian Encyclopedia |date=July 20, 2023}}</ref>

He retired from administrative roles in 1976 to return to lecturing full-time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Erindale's Robinson to retire |url=https://www7.mississauga.ca/documents/library/biographies/Scans/Peel%20Biography%20Scans%20-%20R/Robinson,%20E.%20A.%20(Peter)%20MN%2019760512.pdf |website=mississauga.ca |publisher=City of Mississauga |access-date=December 19, 2025 |date=May 12, 1976}}</ref>

Robinson was awarded a College Award in 1988 for his contributions to Erindale College, and an Arbor Award from the University of Toronto in 2006 for his service to the university.<ref name="Martin_2026">{{cite news |last1=Martin |first1=Kate |title=Former principal and chemist E.A. Peter Robinson remembered as 'founding champion' of Erindale College |url=https://www.utm.utoronto.ca/main-news/former-principal-and-chemist-ea-peter-robinson-remembered-founding-champion-erindale |publisher=University of Toronto Mississauga News |date=August 7, 2026}}</ref>

Robinson died in July 2026 in [[Bristol]], UK, at the age of 93.<ref name="Martin_2026"/>

==Research==
Peter Robinson's research was primarily focused on the chemistry of [[sulphuric acid]]. His work contributed to the invention of [[superacid]]s, pioneered the use of the Toronto Mercury Arc-Lamp, and discovered the proof of [[C–H···O interaction|C–H···O hydrogen bonding]] in [[methanesulfonyl fluoride]].<ref name=scholars>{{cite web |title=Frontiers in Chemistry and Drug Discovery |url=https://scholarsconferences.com/chemistry-frontiers-2019/scientific-committee/edward-a-peter-robinson-dean-at-university-of-toronto-mississauga-canada |website=Scholars International |access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref><ref name=alleyns>{{cite web |title=Alumnus Supports Science |url=https://www.alleyns.org.uk/news/2022-06-17/alumnus-supports-science |website=Alleyn’s School |date=June 17, 2022}}</ref>

==Honours==
The Department of Chemical and Physical Sciences at the [[University of Toronto Mississauga]] hosts a lecture series named in honour of Robinson called the E. A. Robinson Science Education Lectureship.<ref>{{cite web |title=E.A. Robinson Science Education Lectureship |url=https://www.utm.utoronto.ca/cps/events/ea-robinson-science-education-lectureship |website=University of Toronto Mississauga |publisher=Department of Chemical & Physical Sciences |access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref>

The University of Toronto Mississauga also gives out two awards in his honour: the E. A. Robinson Teaching Excellence Award for Senior Faculty, for distinguished undergraduate instructors,<ref>{{cite web |title=E.A. Robinson Teaching Excellence Award for Senior Faculty |url=https://www.viceprovostundergrad.utoronto.ca/vpiue-award/teaching-excellence-award-for-senior-faculty/ |website=University of Toronto |publisher=Office of the Vice-Provost, Innovations in Undergraduate Education |access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> and the E. A. Robinson Medal, for the top graduating student in each of the four major disciplines at the campus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Graduation Awards |url=https://www.utm.utoronto.ca/registrar/finances/awards/graduation |website=University of Toronto Mississauga |access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref>
